subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred turn-maintenance timeouts remain a new opt-in, disabled-by-default configuration setting, or should OpenClaw adopt a supported default/shared safety budget that protects existing affected sessions without operator configuration?
rationale: The branch is intentionally compatible by leaving the bound off, but that policy also leaves the reported user-facing wedge unchanged after upgrade; selecting the default is a maintainer product and compatibility decision, not a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Approve opt-in timeout policy
options.body: Keep the new setting disabled by default and merge with explicit operator-facing documentation for enabling it when maintenance wedges.

options.title: Use an existing shared safety budget
options.body: Rework the branch to use a documented existing compaction/runtime timeout policy so affected existing deployments gain bounded behavior without a new setting.

options.title: Pause for context-engine policy design
options.body: Hold this PR until owners define the desired timeout/default contract for third-party background context engines.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in timeout policy
recommendation.body: Keep the new setting disabled by default and merge with explicit operator-facing documentation for enabling it when maintenance wedges.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the closest available history signal on the same deferred context-engine maintenance lifecycle, though ownership confidence is low without direct main-history inspection.
